risks: Distribution-surface illusion: every channel in config reads 'configured, enabled'. Discord proves that false (401 + restart loop). Any plan that names a surface must first prove reachability with a real call, not a config read.

Contamination risk at publish time: 10/12 articles leak internal proposal/mission/step ids and 5/12 leak internal file paths. Publishing unblocked but ungated puts our internal identifiers and [mock-llm] artifacts in public, and mock ids mean any reported 'reach' is fabricated.

Attention concentration: 172 of 323 queued steps (53%) are postmortems for four dead missions, and 88 observer proposals in 12h target only those four. Every hour this persists is an hour of the ceiling that never reaches content or distribution.
Reputation risk on E3: an unsolicited measurement post to a third-party repo is the one experiment here that can lose access, so it stays human-gated and measurement-only.
Self-referential content drift: 3 of the last 12 articles are about our own postmortems and queue, which is zero audience value if a publish path opens before E1 fixes packaging.

Measurement drift in our own intel: authored-tweet counts are still quoted inconsistently across channels (20/32/34/35 lifetime variants), so all numbers in this artifact were re-measured directly from ops_mission_steps rather than inherited.

Not filing anything upstream tonight: E3 requires human go and E1/E2 must land first.
Not touching the 4 dead missions or their 172 queued postmortems: that is a dedupe decision for the operator, not a growth action.
